Q: How can I take the raw bits of an int32 and create a float32 from them? A:

Note that not all values from the range 0.. 2^32-1 are valid for float:

union { float f; int i; } u;
u.f = -1.f/0; printf("%X = %f\n", u.i, u.f);
u.f = -0.f/0; printf("%X = %f\n", u.i, u.f);
u.f = +0.f/0; printf("%X = %f\n", u.i, u.f);
u.f = +1.f/0; printf("%X = %f\n", u.i, u.f);

The results depend on the compiler, but the meaning is something like this:

FF800000 = -inf
FFC00000 = -nan
7FC00000 = nan
7F800000 = inf

All values with exponent = 11111111 are invalid:

x1111111 1xxxxxxx xxxxxxxx xxxxxxxx

There are 2^24 such numbers out of 2^32 possible. That is, the probability of getting such a number by rand() function is 1/256. They need to be excluded when generating, for example like this:

do u.i = rand(); while ((u.i & 0x7F800000) == 0x7F800000);

Another option is to perform a cyclic shift to the left and consider evenly obtaining a number in the range 0 .. 0xFF000000-1. We can take the remainder of the division:

rand() % 0xFF000000

But then the uniformity of the distribution is violated, since the probability of getting numbers in the range of 0 .. 0x01000000-1 doubles (1/256 -> 1/128).

The transformation of the range also violates the uniformity of the distribution. In this example, the probability of getting 0, 1, 3 is 2 times greater than 2, 4:

(rand() % 8) * 5 / 8

However, I noticed an interesting feature: 32-bit rand() never returns a number 0xFFxxxxxx, and 16-bit rand() never returns a number 0xFFxx. That is, we can simply get the number and shift it cyclically back to the right. This may not be true for all implementations.

Q: error building ios app using React Native Firebase A:

You might want to check your Firebase configuration and make sure the iOS setup steps are completed correctly. Sometimes build errors happen if the GoogleService-Info.plist file is not properly added to the project or linked with the correct target in Xcode.

Also verify that the React Native Firebase packages are installed and linked correctly especially if you are using Expo with a custom development build.

import math

# 1. Create Array1

Q: Generating large amounts of PDF Docs from templates A:

Have a look at iTextSharp. You can use the PdfStamper object to dink with the original PDF and spit out customized versions very quickly. You might need to do a little massaging of the source PDF (define some form obejcts in Acrobat, etc) to get it to do exactly what you want, but it's very high performance compared to the process you're describing. We use it to generate thousands of PDFs a day (with customized info inserted for each customer), and it's free. A little tricky to get your head around (steep learning curve). I'd highly suggest buying the eBook "iText In Action"- the samples there make the whole thing much easier to grok.

Q: Stored Proc and SqlCommand Timeout A:

As brendan stated, the client sends an "abort" and processing stops dead. As simple as that.

However, it's more complex than that...

Any transactions are not rolled back by default and locks are just left there until the connection is closed. If returned to the connection pool and reused, then this does not count as closing.

This is why SET XACT_ABORT ON (other questions SO1, SO2) is recommended

Q: How Do LINQ TO SQL Stored Procedure Calls Work? A:

The stored procedure will get called when you enumerate the result, so the execution is deferred. However, it is not lazily loaded. Meaning, once you enumerate the result of your stored procedure, you will effectively be executing the stored procedure in it's entirety and all the results will be brought back.

If you are binding the results of your stored procedure to a data model class, which supports lazy loading on it's child elements, then you get lazy loading on that class' properties.
